summary: FBYD is a themed entertainment developer with project-based revenue and high fixed costs. Its supply chain depends on creative talent, IP rights, and construction partners, with concentrated exposure to capital availability and demand recovery. Cash runway and talent retention are critical risk factors.

inputs.concentration: High - specialized workers are scarce, turnover disrupts projects
inputs.fragility: High - key departures can halt development

inputs.whyNeeded: Underpins branded attractions and content; disputes or loss could impair revenue
inputs.concentration: Medium - depends on a few major IP partners
inputs.fragility: High - contractual loss or litigation would cripple revenue

inputs.whyNeeded: Build hotels, theme parks, and complexes; fixed costs escalate if delays arise
inputs.concentration: Medium - small pool of specialized themed-construction firms
inputs.fragility: Moderate - labor or material shortages delay projects

inputs.whyNeeded: Fund high fixed costs and project pipeline; ongoing capital needs
inputs.concentration: High - relies on equity/bond issuance (volatile conditions)

chokepoints.why: Project-based revenue is lumpy; any gap forces dilution or project cancellation
Losing lead creatives could stall projects, damage reputation, and hurt IP appeal

consumers.why: Direct customers for designed attractions; demand tied to travel trends
End users of FBYD's themed experiences; growth depends on leisure spending
Drive demand for hospitality/retail/entertainment projects; sensitive to rates

supplyChain.geographic: US headquarters; projects likely domestic and select international markets. Geopolitical risk low but China demand exposure (via Shanghai-industrial comparison headline) implies some Asia exposure.
supplyChain.substitutes: In-house design by competitors (e.g., Disney, Universal); generic construction firms; alternative entertainment formats (streaming, VR). Limited for high-end themed design.

bearCase: FBYD's project-based revenue means lumpy cash flows; if capital markets tighten, it may dilute equity or default. Demand for themed development is cyclical—recession or travel downturn could slash bookings. Loss of a key IP or creative lead would halt projects, worsening cash burn. Stock at $16.9 near 52w high suggests optimism priced in; any earnings miss could trigger sharp drop.

loadBearing.assumption: Company can raise ongoing capital at reasonable cost
loadBearing.breaksIf: Interest rates stay high or credit markets tighten, leading to dilutive equity issuance or project delays
Departure of lead designers/producers would stall projects and harm reputation

loadBearing.assumption: Demand for themed entertainment/hotel development recovers or holds
loadBearing.breaksIf: Recession, travel downturn, or competing attractions reduce project orders

loadBearing.assumption: No major contractual loss or IP dispute
loadBearing.breaksIf: Litigation or IP rights revocation could eliminate major revenue streams

prediction.resolutionCriterion: FBYD reports Q2 2026 earnings; actual revenue vs consensus, and guidance, determines if prediction holds

diminishingReturns: Stopped at construction partners, IP, and talent—no deeper hops needed because the core risk is capital access and talent retention, not raw material supply chains. Further tracing (e.g., steel for construction) would not change the investment picture as fixed costs and demand are the binding constraints.
